title: Republic of Texas
capsule: The Republic of Texas was an independent sovereign state that existed from March 2, 1836 — when delegates at Washington-on-the-Brazos declared independence from Mexico following Santa Anna's suppression of the Texian rebellion — until its annexation by the United States on December 29, 1845. Sam Houston served as the republic's first and third president, navigating severe financial insolvency, continued conflict with Mexico and Comanche raids, and diplomatic non-recognition by most European powers. The republic claimed an expansive territory extending to the Rio Grande and even to the upper Arkansas River, claims Mexico never conceded, and the resulting boundary dispute contributed directly to the Mexican-American War (1846–1848).
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The republic's claimed territory is well-documented through official proclamations, but effective control extended only over a fraction of those claims, making the map footprint dependent on which definition of sovereignty is applied.
